title: Run a swarm of agents to solve security challenges
summary: N1nEmAn reports a Claude-driven commander-and-worker agent legion won a Tencent attack-defense contest, scoring 85 flags on 1B tokens versus the runner-up's 4.5B.
agent_role: An AI commander reads the board and dispatches tasks; general and soldier agents attack targets in parallel; a script watchdog keeps them alive. Humans built the foundation and steered iteration.
outcome: Author reports first place in a 634-team qualifier, 85 flags scored, 25 seconds faster than the runner-up using 1B tokens versus 4.5B.
what_they_did: The author built a multi-agent system for authorized security testing. An AI commander spawns worker agents in terminal panes, assigns targets, and stores lessons in a layered fact graph. Light models do mass work, strong models decide. It ran unattended for 8 hours in a Tencent contest.
how_it_went: The author says the system won the online qualifier with 85 flags on 1 billion tokens, beating a runner-up that used 4.5 billion, and invented roles like a flag-collecting signalman on its own.
worth_knowing: This is for authorized security testing only; the repo includes a disclaimer and a proposed marking scheme to limit abuse.
prompt: Set up a team of AI agents for an authorized security testing exercise on [target scope you are permitted to test]. Use one commander agent to read the current state and dispatch worker agents, and keep a shared notes file where agents record what they learn. Have the commander show its plan and wait for my approval before any action against a system. Only act within the scope I confirm in writing.

curation.rationale: Detailed, documented multi-agent pentest system that won a competition with a specific token-efficiency result; novel but security-sensitive and partly manifesto.
